Decide whether a string is a valid ISBN-10, with or without dashes.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/isbn-verifier) (MIT). Listed under [Parsing & Validation](/examples/?subject=parsing-and-validation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: isbn_verifier.nomi
//# Checks ISBN-10 numbers.

/// Reports whether `isbn` is a valid ISBN-10: nine digits and a check
/// character, a digit or `X` for 10, with dashes allowed anywhere, whose
/// digits weighted 10 down to 1 sum to a multiple of 11.
pub fn is_valid(isbn: String) -> Bool {
    values =
        isbn
        |> String.replace("-", "")
        |> Iter.with_index()
        |> Iter.map(fn #(i, character) -> value(character, is_check: i == 9))
        |> Maybe.collect()

    case values {
        Some(values) when Iter.count(values) == 10 -> checksum(values) % 11 == 0
        _ -> False
    }
}

/// The value of one ISBN character: a digit, or `X` for 10 in the check
/// position.
fn value(character: String, is_check: Bool) -> Maybe<Int> {
    case character {
        "X" when is_check -> Some(10)
        _ -> String.to_int(character)
    }
}

fn checksum(values: List<Int>) -> Int {
    values
    |> Iter.with_index()
    |> Iter.map(fn #(i, v) -> v * (10 - i))
    |> Iter.sum()
}

// FILE: isbn_verifier_test.nomi
import isbn_verifier

test "verifies ISBN-10 numbers" {
    cases = [
        #("valid isbn", "3-598-21508-8", True),
        #("invalid isbn check digit", "3-598-21508-9", False),
        #("valid isbn with a check digit of 10", "3-598-21507-X", True),
        #("check digit is a character other than X", "3-598-21507-A", False),
        #("invalid check digit in isbn is not treated as zero", "4-598-21507-B", False),
        #("invalid character in isbn is not treated as zero", "3-598-P1581-X", False),
        #("X is only valid as a check digit", "3-598-2X507-9", False),
        #("only one check digit is allowed", "3-598-21508-96", False),
        #("X is not substituted by the value 10", "3-598-2X507-5", False),
        #("valid isbn without separating dashes", "3598215088", True),
        #("isbn without separating dashes and X as check digit", "359821507X", True),
        #("isbn without check digit and dashes", "359821507", False),
        #("too long isbn and no dashes", "3598215078X", False),
        #("too short isbn", "00", False),
        #("isbn without check digit", "3-598-21507", False),
        #("check digit of X should not be used for 0", "3-598-21515-X", False),
        #("empty isbn", "", False),
        #("input is 9 characters", "134456729", False),
        #("invalid characters are not ignored after checking length", "3132P34035", False),
        #("invalid characters are not ignored before checking length", "3598P215088", False),
        #("input is too long but contains a valid isbn", "98245726788", False),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, isbn, expected), description {
        assert isbn_verifier.is_valid(isbn) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Dashes are removed first, then each grapheme becomes a value with its position from `Iter.with_index`, and `Maybe.collect` makes one `Maybe<List<Int>>`. A character that is neither a digit nor a check-position `X` makes the whole ISBN invalid in that one step.
- `value` takes the position as a named Bool, `value(character, is_check: i == 9)`, so the `case` arm reads `"X" when is_check -> Some(10)`.
- The length rule is a `when` guard on the `Some` arm, as in luhn, rather than a separate `if` before the conversion. The weights come from the index too, `v * (10 - i)`.
- All 21 cases are one `subtests` table.
